title: Black Leopard, Red Wolf
author: Marlon James
review:
I only read the first part of this book, but I do feel like it's earned a review warning away everyone from it. This is the most depraved and disgusting book I've read and I don't really feel like there's a deeper meaning to any of it. I've read some very dark books and series but usually they have a point behind the darkness or at least give you moments of reprieve, this book really doesn't and there's some new level of depravity it finds every chapter / page / sentence that is really uncomfortable and is seemingly forgotten in a short amount of time and has no impact on the characters and setting.

Nicest thing I can say about this book is I thought the writing at points was quite good and there were some weird dreamlike sequences that were interesting.

I don't know, maybe I don't get it, but I feel like as an enjoyer of dark weird books if I don't really like this book I'd want to heavily discourage anyone else from reading it.

highlights.text: Bi oju ri enu a pamo. Not everything the eye sees should be spoken by the mouth.

The last man was a boy. He cried. He was too shaken to beg for his life. I told him to be a man in his next life, for he is less than a worm in this one, and flung the knife right into his neck. His blood hit the floor before his knees.
I let the half-blind man live because we need stories in order to live, don’t we, priest? Inquisitor. I don’t know what to call you.
Sometimes the only way forward is through. So I walked through. I was not afraid.
Write what you see; be it witchcraft, be it white science, my eye is whatever you think it is. I have no guise. I have no look.
I was a fool. I thought you learned the old ways by forgetting the new.
back then I still thought there was a self to lose, not knowing that one never owns the self.
“The only way to inside your head is I cut open and look, or you speak it out.”

I looked as high as I could look and walked as far as I could walk. Not only was sun still behind the branches and leaves, but this trunk was without end. By the time I walked around it, I forgot where it began.
The ground was right now not the ground, and the sky was not the sky, and lie was truth and truth was a shifting, slithering thing. Truth was making me sick.
“Fuck the gods, for now I feel like I can skip on air,”

I thought if I stayed here much longer I would turn myself into a Gangatom, and start killing until there was a hole in the village as big as the hole I see when I close my eyes. A dead thing never lies, cheats, or betrays, and what was a family but a place where all three bloom like moss.
You only need to be told down is up for down to change.

Everywhere looked as if another giant finger was going to push through the ground, followed by a hand and an arm and a green man taller than five hundred houses. Green and green-brown and dark green, and a green that was blue, and a green that was yellow. A forest of them.

My legs burned when we finally broke into sky. The clouds were thin as cold breath and the sun, yellow and hungry. In front of us, it floated on the mist. Truth, it stood on branches but the walls were set against the trunk, and had the same flowers, and moss. A house set in the tree with colours of the mountain.
Fear blood sauces their brews.

Like, I like. Dislike, I love. Disgust, I can feel. Loathing, I can grab in the palm of my hand and squeeze. And hatred, I can live in hatred for days. But the smug smile of indifference on someone’s face makes me want to hack it off.
You know me, but I know you too. I could smell everything about you before you came down those steps.
“Maybe what you need to cut away is the foolish wisdom of men who still make walls with cow shit.”
“So you either speak through your ass or fart through your mouth.
